1 قَحَدَ , aor.
قَحَدَ , (K,) inf. n. قَحْدٌ; (K, * TK;) and ↓ اقحد ; (TA;) He (a camel) became in the state of having a قَحَدَة [q. v.], (K, TA,) meaning, a hump like a cupola; so accord. to ISd: (TA:) or became large in the قحدة, (K, TA,) after smallness [thereof]: (TA:) and قَحَدَتْ, inf. n. قُحُودٌ; and قَحِدَتْ; (IKtt, L;) and ↓ اقحدت ; (S, IKtt, L;) she (a camel) became in the state of having a قَحَدَة: (ISd, L:) or became large in her hump; (S, IKtt;) [i. e.] became such as is termed مِقْحَاد; (L;) [and] so ↓ استحقدت : (A, TA: *) or ↓ اقحدت signifies she continued always to have a قحدة, even when she had become lean. (L.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
